segments.he: וְהַמּוֹצֵא מְצִיאָה לֹא יִשָּׁבַע. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: ״שְׁנֵי כִּיסִין קְשׁוּרִין מָצָאתָ לִי״; וְהַלָּה אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא מָצָאתִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד״ – נִשְׁבָּע. ״שְׁנֵי שְׁוָורִים קְשׁוּרִין מָצָאתָ לִי״; וְהַלָּה אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא אֶחָד״ – אֵינוֹ נִשְׁבָּע.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And» it was further instituted that «one who finds a lost item» and returns it to its rightful owner is «not» required to «take an oath» that he did not keep any part of the lost item for himself. This ordinance was also instituted for the betterment of the world. «Rabbi Yitzḥak says:» If the owner of the lost item brings a claim against the finder, saying: «You found two» money «pouches tied» together that belong «to me, and the other» person «says: I found only one» pouch, then the finder «takes an oath,» similar to anyone who admits to part of a claim. If the owner claims: «You found two oxen tied» together that belong «to me, and the other» person «says: There was only one» ox, the finder is «not» required to «take an oath.»

moves.about: the mishna's rule that a finder does not take an oath

positions.claim: finder who admits one of two tied pouches swears; of two tied oxen he does not
